hook: 131 cuneiform tablets unearthed at Kayalıpınar reveal a forgotten plague.

sections.voiceover: 131 cuneiform tablets unearthed at Kayalıpınar reveal a forgotten plague.
sections.visual_cue: A pile of 131 ancient tablets on a desert dig site, with a faint plague symbol overlay.

sections.voiceover: Archaeologists uncovered 131 tablets at Kayalıpınar, dating to about 1300 BC. Now the archive holds 184 tablets, the largest Hittite cache found. Which childhood fever epidemic do these tablets record?
sections.visual_cue: Map of central Turkey highlighting Kayalıpınar, then a shelf of 184 tablets, ending on a close‑up of a tablet showing a fever glyph.

sections.voiceover: But the tablets also detail a plague that killed thousands of children.
sections.visual_cue: Illustration of sick children beside a tablet panel depicting a burning sun motif.

sections.voiceover: The tablets note a fever epidemic that hit Hittite Empire 3,400 years ago. It mainly killed infants, reshaping court life. Minister Mehmet Nuri Ersoy announced the find on 16 Oct 2026, the largest Hittite archive.
sections.visual_cue: Timeline bar marking 3,400 years, a scene of a royal court, and a news‑style shot of Minister Ersoy at a press podium.

sections.voiceover: 131 tablets now illuminate a forgotten Hittite plague.
sections.visual_cue: Slow zoom on a single tablet with the plague glyph glowing.
